Subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval follow-up

Sara — thanks for the call this morning, appreciate the time. Quick recap + next steps so we’re aligned: 

Highlights from our discussion:
- Workload: steady-burst at peak office hours, expected ~800-1,200 concurrent inference connections for chat; large embedding batches overnight (~50k/day).
- Latency SLO: target p99 <= 150ms for chat flows (90% of traffic); bulk embed latency can be slower.
- Availability: you need predictable capacity during product launches (hard dates for Q3).
- Procurement: procurement wants capacity guarantees and clear reserved pricing + SLA language.

What we’ll deliver next:
1) Test plan for a Dedicated POC (load profile + synthetic test harness).
2) Sample benchmark numbers vs hyperscaler-hosted endpoints for a representative model and sequence length.
3) Reserved capacity quote + suggested SLA/contract language for capacity guarantees.
4) Mutual action plan template to track milestones (I attached a starter MA template).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf (quick product brief), ma-template.xlsx (mutual action plan).

Proposed next timestep: 30-45 minute POC kickoff next week to align on the exact model variant and test windows — what is your availability Tuesday/Wednesday morning PT?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa and Dylan to own the test and pricing follow-ups.

Best,

- For hyperscaler comparison, procurement wants a clear cost and capacity comparison against reserved GPU instances (we're looking at GCP A2/A3 options and AWS p4d-like offerings).

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval follow-up — proposed POC and test plan

Sara — looping back with an initial POC/test plan and notes on Dedicated vs hyperscaler tradeoffs. Happy to walk through live.

POC test plan (high level):
- Target window: 2-day test window during off-peak hours we agree on.
- Workload: 1,000 concurrent sessions (chat), steady arrival rate with 95th percentile session length ~12 tokens per request; bulk embed batch tests overnight with 50k items.
- Model variants: run the same model in three modes: 1) FP16 (baseline), 2) int8 quantized, 3) server-side optimized distilled variant (if you prefer lower latencies).
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1k requests.
- Hyperscaler comparison: we’ll run identical synthetic workload against a hyperscaler-managed endpoint (we can provision AWS/GCP instances that match your estimate) to provide apples-to-apples p99 and cost numbers.

Key Dedicated differentiators (what Nova Labs told us you care about):
- Guaranteed reserved pools: Redwood Dedicated supports reserved GPU pools with capacity isolation for committed contracts. For committed capacity we can provide throughput guarantees tied to the reserved pool size.
- Autoscaling and burst: Dedicated includes configurable autoscaling and burst policies; we can restrict or enable burst-to-hosted to meet launch windows.
- Unified runtime optimizations: our serving runtime gives consistent latency across model variants and supports aggressive KV/prefix caching to reduce tail latency vs generic cloud setups.
- Contract/SLAs: we can provide contract language that includes capacity commitment, lead times for additional capacity, and remedies (service credits) if reserved capacity wasn’t available. Exact SLA language needs legal/pricing review.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Dylan: please confirm a reserved capacity quote for a 6-month commit (N GPUs) + proposed SLA text for capacity guarantees.
2) Sara/procurement: if you can share any specific contract redlines up front it will speed legal review.
3) Align on POC dates (we can run the synthetic comparison and return results within 5 business days of the test window).

Attachments: test-plan.md (detailed steps), benchmark-results-sample.csv (sample from a recent customer POC).

I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff to walk through the plan once Dylan posts the pricing/SLA.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
